content.title: Duke’s Cameron Boozer earns Sporting News 2025-26 Player of the Year
content.text: March 12, 2026, 1:16 p.m. ETDuke freshman Cameron Boozer was named the 2025-26 College Basketball Player of the Year by Sporting News.Boozer averaged 22.7 points and 10.2 rebounds, leading the Blue Devils to a 29-2 record.He was recognized for his polished, veteran-like approach and extensive history of winning championships.Boozer is also a Sporting News first-team All-America selection and is expected to be a top pick in the upcoming NBA Draft.Following a stellar freshman season, Duke’s Cameron Boozer has been named the 2025-26 College Basketball Player of the Year by Sporting News Thursday. Boozer averaged 22.7 points and 10.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 1.5 steals over 31 games, leading Duke to a 29-2 record.In a season featuring a wealth of talent, especially among the freshman class, Boozer stood out not only as a high-level producer but also as a player polished well beyond his years, at times looking like a senior in his approach to the game.Cameron Boozer’s maturity has fueled Duke’s successThat veteran attitude and his proclivity to winning basketball were among the top reasons Boozer was selected for the honor, according to Sporting News. Citing his rich history of success as a four-time state champion, a three-time Nike Peach Jam champion and a U16 and U17 United States FIBA Americas Champion."I played against almost every top guy – whether it's with my high-school team, my AAU team or at camps," Boozer said in a quote provided to Sporting News. "We played basically with or against almost everyone. Everyone talked about our class being a great class before we even got to college. I'm sure we exceeded expectations. I obviously had a lot of confidence in myself coming into the year. So, yeah, I'm not surprised by how great our freshman class is playing."Coming off a season that featured the stellar play of Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel, Khaman Maluach, and more, it would have been understandably difficult to replicate the success the team saw after losing those three talents, plus Sion James and Tyrese Proctor, who were both significant contributors. Despite this, Boozer led the Blue Devils to an additional regular-season win, including a record-setting 11 wins over AP-ranked teams.Though he is expected to be among the first players to hear their name called in the upcoming NBA Draft, the collegiate storybook is far from over for Boozer, as the ACC and NCAA tournaments are still to come, as are the accolades.Boozer was recently named among Sporting News first-team All-America selections, alongside Arkansas' Darius Acuff Jr., BYU's AJ Dybansta, Iowa State's Joshua Jefferson, and Michigan's Yaxel Lendeborg. As the NCAA’s award season continues, many more honors are expected for Boozer.Follow us @DukeWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Duke Blue Devils news, notes, and opinions.
